decisions.reason: Turn 3 uses 'You are Mr. Sun?' as a confirmation question and turn 23 directly addresses B as 'Mr. Sun', establishing B's name.
Turn 5: 'I have read your resume' uses definite possessive 'your resume', directly establishing B has a resume.
Turn 5: 'I know you have worked for 3 years' is a direct assertion about B's work experience based on the resume.
Turn 5: 'Why did you choose to major in mechanical engineering?' is a why-question presupposing B chose to major in mechanical engineering.

decisions.claim: B is interested in mechanical engineering
decisions.reason: Turn 7: 'What are you primarily interested in about mechanical engineering?' presupposes B has primary interests in mechanical engineering.
decisions.counterexample: B might say 'I'm not really interested in any particular aspect' but the question structure presupposes interest exists.

decisions.reason: Turn 9: 'Why did you decide to apply for this position?' presupposes B applied for a position. Supported by turn 13's mention of applicants.

decisions.claim: B is one of several applicants for the position
decisions.reason: Turn 13: 'We have several applicants for this position' combined with B being interviewed for that position establishes B is one of several applicants.
Turn 23: 'I'll let you know the result of the interview' directly states B participated in an interview.
Identical claim to c1 (B's name is Mr. Sun) with same evidence. c1 is the canonical statement.

decisions.claim: B has a resume that was read by the interviewer
decisions.reason: Same core fact as c2 (B has a resume). The addition 'read by the interviewer' is merely restating turn 5's content and doesn't add a distinct property of B.

decisions.claim: B applied for a position at the company where A works
decisions.reason: Subsumed by c6 (B applied for a position) plus c7 (position at this company). The 'at the company where A works' is supported by turn 11's 'such as ours' but doesn't constitute a separate B-attribute beyond c6 and c7.

decisions.claim: B is one of several applicants for this position
decisions.reason: Identical claim to c7 (B is one of several applicants for this position) with same evidence.

decisions.claim: B asked at least one question about the job during the interview
decisions.reason: Turn 17 asks 'Have you anything to ask about the job?' and turn 19 begins with 'Yes' (addressing B's question), confirming B asked at least one question.

decisions.claim: B asked more than one question about the job
decisions.reason: Turn 19 confirms B asked a question, and turn 21 'Anything else?' implies B asked more than one (A is inviting further questions after the first was answered).
decisions.counterexample: B could have said 'No' to 'Anything else?' but the structure implies at least one additional question was asked before turn 21.

decisions.claim: B gave an answer that A found positive before the career development question
decisions.reason: Turn 15: 'That sounds very good' is A's positive evaluation of B's prior answer, immediately before asking about career development. This establishes B gave an answer A found positive.
